messages.subject: Interesting bug in update_geom_defaults
parts:
Well, at least a very interesting design feature!

I have spent some time creating my own default colour schemes in
geoms, using the update_geom_defaults() function. This works very
well indeed, but I stumbled upon a minor bug.

My use-case is that I want to define a variable with the name of the
new default geom colour, and then run update_geom_defaults() once for
each geom I want to update in this way. This saves a little bit of
typing if you want to update many geoms.

So far, so good.

I always test my code to ensure it is repeatable by clearing the
entire workspace, e.g. by pressing the 'clear all' button in Tinn-R,
equivalent to rm(list=ls(all=TRUE)).

My expectation is that this resets the entire system to a blank state,
so this should then reset the geom default colours to the factory
fresh state... But wait, what actually happens is R throws an error
and stops.

The reason is that I have passed the colour as a variable into
update_geom_defaults(). I don't understand enough about the internal
workings of eval() to be able to trace the problem any further, and
unfortunately can't propose a patch.

Anyway, this little "design feature" has a really interesting side-
effects. It means you can update the default colour by changing the
value of the variable, without calling update_geom_defaults() again!
This is so neat, that it would almost be a shame to fix this ;-P

This is better explained by some code:

Enjoy

Andrie

--

library(ggplot2)

# Update the default geom colour
default_colour <- "red"
update_geom_defaults("bar", aes(fill=default_colour))

# Create dummy data and plot
x <- rnorm(50)*10
qplot(x, geom="bar", binwidth=1) # This works

# Now clear everything in the workspace
# (Equivalent to pressing 'clear all' button in Tinn-R)
rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))

# Rereate dummy data and plot
x <- rnorm(50)*10
qplot(x, geom="bar", binwidth=1) # This throws an error and stops


# This has some interesting side-effects
default_colour <- "green"
update_geom_defaults("bar", aes(fill=default_colour))

qplot(x, geom="bar", binwidth=1) # Plot in green

default_colour <- "blue"
qplot(x, geom="bar", binwidth=1) # You didn't expect this, did you?

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Interesting bug in update_geom_defaults
parts:
Hi Andrie,

This seems to be a mistake in the examples - you actually want

update_geom_defaults("bar", aes_string(fill=default_colour))

which will behave as you expect.

Hadley
